title: include: add the c128 128-bit arithmetic logic unit^Winclude library.
description:
From Michael Clark's https://github.com/michaeljclark/c128; it provides
a "128-bit integer type with logic, shifts, arithmetic and bitmanip."

It is not yet used; the initial use will be for some places that have
128-bit time stamps; it could also be used for FT_{INT,UINT}128 types,
for example.

It's a header-only library, with #defines, type definitions, and static
inline routines.

This is the header files from that project with no changes other than
adding the copyright notice from integer.h to the other header files,
adding an SPDX entry after the copyright notice, and removing some
end-of-line whitespace, as the Wireshark builders require that.  This
establishes a baseline for any changes necessary to fit into Wireshark.

The LICENSE file for c128 claims, at the top, that it's the MIT license,
but the text in that file, and in integer.h, is closer to the ISC
license - https://opensource.org/license/isc-license-txt - than to the
MIT license - https://opensource.org/license/MIT. The *only* difference
between the license text here and the ISC license is that the first
sentence in the ISC license says "and/or" rather than "and". Thus, the
SPDX code here is ISC, not MIT.


(cherry picked from commit eaf3bc2d7d5c446851ea4a75e1ff7a5570eac6c7)

Co-authored-by: Guy Harris <gharris@sonic.net>

> Please note the discussion on the licence text right at the point mentioned: https://www.gnu.org/licenses/license-list.en.html#ISC

It says

> This license had an unfortunate wording choice: it provided recipients with “Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software…” This was the same language from the license of Pine that the University of Washington later claimed prohibited people from distributing modified versions of the software.
> 
> ISC has told us they do not share the University of Washington's interpretation, and we have every reason to believe them. ISC also updated the license to read “Permission to use, copy, modify, **and/or** distribute this software…” ...

The author of c128 might have grabbed a version of the pre-change ISC license.
